tasks.title: Packet period
tasks.solution: T = 1/f. For 250 Hz it is 4 ms; that is the lower bound of the radio link's latency.

tasks.title: Telemetry rate
tasks.solution: f_telem = rate / N. One of N slots is given to the reply, which is why telemetry is always slower than control.

tasks.title: Margin to the sensitivity threshold
tasks.solution: Margin = RSSI − the mode's sensitivity threshold. Each mode has its own threshold: −96 dBm is a 12 dB margin at 250 Hz (−108) and only 9 dB at 500 Hz (−105). The OSD warning is set 5–10 dB above the threshold.

tasks.title: Range when changing mode
tasks.solution: The gain is Δ = a − b dB, and range grows as 10^(Δ/20): +4 dB (250 → 150 Hz) is ×1.58, +7 dB (250 → 50 Hz) ×2.24, +10 dB (500 → 50 Hz) ×3.16. This is the other side of the "−3 dB = ×0.71" rule.

tasks.title: Range at a required margin
tasks.solution: The current margin is M = RSSI − S; the excess over the requirement is Δ = M − M_req. In free space range grows as 10^(Δ/20): 6 dB ≈ ×2. Example: 1 km, −80 dBm, 250Hz (−108), a 12 dB margin → Δ = 16 dB → ×6.31 → 6.3 km. Reality is usually 5–10 dB worse (rf-link-budget): a 6 dB correction halves the result.

tasks.title: Model Match: the UID5 byte in SYNC
tasks.solution: tx_main.cpp:411–415: UID5 ^= (~modelId) & 0x3F. Only the low 6 bits change; the high 2 stay, and the receiver uses them to establish the link, but outputs channels only if the whole byte matches. Example: UID5 = 38, ID 1 → ¬1 AND 63 = 62 → 38 XOR 62 = 24; ID 5 → 38 XOR 58 = 28.
